questions.text: What is the zero conditional used for, according to Reading 1?
questions.correct: Universal facts and automatic consequences
questions.hint: "The zero conditional is used for universal truths and automatic consequences." ✅

questions.text: What makes the first conditional different from the second?
opts: First is about past, second about future
questions.correct: First = realistic possibility; second = hypothetical/unlikely
questions.hint: "The first conditional: the speaker genuinely believes this is achievable." Second = "invites the listener to imagine an alternative reality." ✅

questions.text: What does the third conditional describe?
opts: Past as it did not happen — counterfactual
questions.correct: Past as it did not happen — counterfactual
questions.hint: "The third conditional takes this further, moving into the purely counterfactual — the past as it did not happen." ✅

questions.text: "If I had taken the scholarship, I would be in Berlin now." — This is:
questions.correct: Mixed: past condition + present result
questions.hint: "had taken" (past PP) + "would be NOW" (present) = mixed conditional connecting past condition to present result. ✅

questions.text: Daniyar says: "If his father's condition hadn't stabilised, he would have deferred." This is:
opts: Third conditional — counterfactual (his father did stabilise)
questions.correct: Third conditional — counterfactual (his father did stabilise)
questions.hint: His father DID stabilise — this imagines the alternative past that didn't happen. Third conditional. ✅

questions.text: In the seminar, which student used second conditional?
questions.correct: Amir — for national coordination hypothetical
questions.hint: "If every university were to introduce courses simultaneously..." — Amir's hypothetical national coordination. Second conditional. ✅

questions.text: "If I speak Czech, I can access legal archives." — Daniyar's zero conditional means:
opts: He is planning to speak Czech
Automatic factual relationship: speaking Czech = accessing archives
questions.correct: Automatic factual relationship: speaking Czech = accessing archives
questions.hint: Present + Present = zero conditional. Factual, automatic relationship. ✅

questions.text: What was wrong with Rustam's first attempt at zero conditional?
opts: He said "will be" — making it first conditional instead of zero
questions.correct: He said "will be" — making it first conditional instead of zero
questions.hint: "You said 'will be' — that's first conditional: a prediction." Zero requires Present Simple in both clauses. ✅

questions.text: What makes Kamila's final seminar sentence a mixed conditional?
opts: Past if-clause (had been introduced) + present result (would already have now)
It uses past perfect in the result
questions.correct: Past if-clause (had been introduced) + present result (would already have now)
questions.hint: "If the module had been introduced earlier" (PP/3rd) + "would already have a foundation NOW" (present/2nd) = mixed Type A. ✅

questions.text: What advice would Daniyar give his 18-year-old self?
opts: Trust the discomfort; don't call home every day
questions.correct: Trust the discomfort; don't call home every day
questions.hint: "Trust the discomfort. If things were easy from the start, they wouldn't be worth doing. Don't call home every day."

questions.text: Zhibek said: "If WKU had introduced this module five years ago, graduates would have been better prepared." — This is:
questions.correct: Third conditional
questions.hint: "had introduced" (PP) + "would have been prepared" (would have + pp) = third conditional. Both past. ✅

questions.text: "If I speak Czech, I can access archives" uses first conditional.
questions.correct: False
questions.hint: Present + Present = ZERO conditional (factual relationship). NOT first conditional. ✅

questions.text: "If you WILL study, you will pass." — What is wrong?
opts: "will study" in if-clause → should be "study" (Present Simple)
questions.correct: "will study" in if-clause → should be "study" (Present Simple)
questions.hint: ✅ "If you STUDY, you will pass." NEVER "will" in the if-clause. ✅

questions.text: "If I ___ (be) you, I ___ (apply) immediately." (second conditional)
questions.correct: were / would apply
questions.hint: Second conditional: IF + WERE + would + base. "If I WERE you, I WOULD APPLY." ✅

questions.text: "If I would have studied, I would have passed." — What is wrong?
opts: "would have studied" in if-clause → should be "had studied"
questions.correct: "would have studied" in if-clause → should be "had studied"
questions.hint: ✅ "If I HAD STUDIED..." — if-clause of 3rd conditional: PAST PERFECT only. ✅

questions.text: "I wish I knew the answer." — This means:
opts: I will know the answer soon
I do NOT know the answer now — contrary to present reality
I knew it in the past
questions.correct: I do NOT know the answer now — contrary to present reality
questions.hint: Wish + Past Simple = contrary to present reality. "I wish I knew" = I DON'T know now. ✅

questions.text: "If she ___ (not / leave) early, she ___ (miss) the train."(3rd cond.)
questions.correct: hadn't left / would have missed
questions.hint: 3rd conditional: "If she HADN'T LEFT early, she WOULD HAVE MISSED the train." ✅

questions.text: "Unless you submit by Friday, you will fail." — "Unless" means:
questions.correct: "If you don't submit"
questions.hint: "unless" = "if not." "Unless you submit" = "IF YOU DON'T SUBMIT." ✅

questions.text: "If I had taken the offer, I would be in Singapore now." — Type:
questions.correct: Mixed: past condition → present result (A)
questions.hint: "had taken" (PP/3rd) + "would be NOW" (present/2nd) = Mixed Type A: past condition → present result. ✅

questions.text: "Had I known about this, I would have responded." — "Had I known" is:
opts: Formal inversion of 3rd conditional (= "If I had known")
questions.correct: Formal inversion of 3rd conditional (= "If I had known")
questions.hint: "Had I known..." = formal inversion. No "if" needed. ✅

questions.text: "Conditional thinking is a feature of human cognition." "Cognition" means:
opts: Mental processes of knowing and understanding
questions.correct: Mental processes of knowing and understanding
questions.hint: "cognition" = the mental processes of acquiring knowledge, understanding, and thinking.

questions.text: "The benefit of hindsight." "Hindsight" means:
opts: Understanding a situation only after it has occurred
questions.correct: Understanding a situation only after it has occurred
questions.hint: "hindsight" = understanding that comes AFTER the event, not before.

questions.text: "If the intervention were effective." "Intervention" means:
opts: A deliberate action to change an outcome
questions.correct: A deliberate action to change an outcome
questions.hint: "intervention" = a deliberate action taken to improve or change a situation.

questions.text: "The causal relationship between X and Y." "Causal" means:
questions.correct: Related to cause and effect
questions.hint: "causal" = relating to cause and effect; what causes what to happen.

questions.text: "This is not idle speculation." "Idle speculation" means:
opts: Useless guessing without real basis or purpose
questions.correct: Useless guessing without real basis or purpose
questions.hint: "idle speculation" = unproductive guessing; thinking without evidence or serious purpose.
